01: Not dangerous goods, but live animals are special cargo: airlines follow the IATA Live Animals Regulations, and you need health certificates and approved containers.
02: Not DG. Perishable: reefer containers by sea, cool chain by air. Chilled air shipments sometimes use dry ice, which is DG (UN1845).
03: Not DG. Perishable: reefer by sea, chilled or frozen by air. Dry ice packing (UN1845) makes an air shipment DG.
04: Not DG. Most items are perishable and need temperature control.
05: Usually general cargo. Some items need veterinary or CITES papers.
06: Not DG. Perishable, and needs a phytosanitary certificate.
07: Not DG. Fresh produce is perishable (reefer or cool chain).
08: Not DG. Fresh fruit is perishable. Note: copra (dried coconut, heading 1203) is DG by sea (UN1363, Class 4.2).
09: Usually general cargo. Spice oleoresins are under chapter 13 and essential oils under 3301, which can be DG.
10: General cargo. Lines may ask for fumigation certificates.
12: Most seeds are general cargo, but copra (UN1363, Class 4.2) and castor beans (UN2969, Class 9) are dangerous goods.
13: Usually general cargo. Oleoresins or extracts that still contain solvent can be flammable (Class 3): check the MSDS.
15: Animal and vegetable fats and oils
Edible and vegetable oils are usually not DG. Some lines still ask for an MSDS or a non-hazardous declaration for oils in flexitanks or drums.
16: General cargo; frozen items need reefer or cool chain.
21: Usually general cargo. Flavourings with alcohol or solvents are under 3302 and can be DG.
22: Water, juices, beer and wine are general cargo. Spirits above 24% alcohol and ethanol are flammable liquids (Class 3).
23: Oil cakes and seed cake (UN1386 / UN2217, Class 4.2) and fishmeal (UN2216 / UN1374) can be dangerous goods. Lines usually ask for oil and moisture certificates.
24: General cargo. E-cigarettes and vapes are chapter 85 and contain lithium batteries.
25: Mostly general cargo. Sulphur can be Class 4.1 (UN1350), and asbestos is Class 9 (UN2212 / UN2590).
26: Most ores in containers are general cargo. Exceptions: radioactive ores (Class 7), zinc ash (UN1435) and aluminium dross (UN3170), which react with water.
27: Fuels, solvents and gases are dangerous goods (Class 2 or 3). Lubricating oils, waxes and solid bitumen are usually not, but lines want the MSDS.
28: Many inorganic chemicals are DG (acids, alkalis, oxidisers, gases). Many others are not. Classification must come from the MSDS.
29: Solvents, alcohols, ketones and many intermediates are DG. Many solid organics and APIs are not. Classification must come from the MSDS.
30: Finished medicines are usually general cargo, but temperature-controlled. Exceptions: products in flammable solvents, aerosols, dry-ice packing and biological samples (UN3373).
31: Urea and most NPK and DAP are usually not DG. Ammonium nitrate and potassium nitrate fertilisers are oxidisers (Class 5.1).
32: Solvent-based paints, varnishes and inks are Class 3 (UN1263 / UN1210). Water-based products and most dyes and pigments are not DG.
33: Perfumes and many essential oils are flammable (UN1266 / UN1169 / UN1197), and sprays are aerosols (UN1950). Creams, lotions and powders are usually not DG.
34: Usually general cargo. Strong cleaners (corrosive) and solvent polishes can be DG.
35: Solvent-based adhesives are Class 3 (UN1133). Water-based glues, gelatin and enzymes are usually not DG.
36: Dangerous goods. Explosives and fireworks are Class 1 and need a PESO licence, and many carriers refuse them. Matches are Class 4.1.
37: Films and plates are general cargo. Some processing chemicals are DG.
38: Pesticides, thinners, fuel additives and many industrial chemicals are DG. Activated carbon and biodiesel need a check.
39: Plastic granules and articles are general cargo. Exceptions: expandable polystyrene beads (UN2211), liquid epoxy resins (often UN3082) and resin solutions in solvent (UN1866).
40: General cargo, including tyres. Rubber solution (adhesive) is Class 3 (UN1287).
41: General cargo. Wet-salted hides may face line restrictions on odour or leakage.
44: Wood is general cargo; wooden packaging needs ISPM-15. Charcoal (4402) is DG Class 4.2 (UN1361), and many lines refuse it.
52: Pressed cotton bales and yarn are normally not DG. Loose or oily cotton and wet cotton can be Class 4.1 / 4.2 (UN3360, UN1364, UN1365).
53: Usually general cargo when baled and dry.
63: General cargo. Used clothing needs import permissions at destination.
68: General cargo; heavy slabs may be out-of-gauge.
71: Not DG, but valuable cargo: special handling, secure storage and insurance.
72: General cargo. Exceptions: some ferro-alloys (ferrosilicon UN1408) and self-heating turnings and borings (UN2793). Scrap is checked for radiation.
73: General cargo. Gas cylinders that are filled, or used and uncleaned, are DG.
76: General cargo. Aluminium powder (UN1309 / UN1396) and dross (UN3170) are DG.
79: General cargo. Zinc dust and powder are DG (UN1436).
81: Solid metal is usually not DG, but powders, turnings and sponge of magnesium, titanium, zirconium and similar metals are flammable solids.
82: General cargo. Cordless tools with lithium batteries are chapter 84 / 85 and need a battery check.
84: Most machinery is general cargo. It becomes DG when it contains fuel (UN3528 / UN3530), refrigerant gas (UN2857 / UN3358), lithium batteries or fire-suppression cylinders.
85: Anything with lithium batteries (phones, laptops, power banks, e-cigarettes) is DG for air and sea (UN3480 / UN3481 / UN3090 / UN3091). Wet lead-acid batteries are Class 8.
86: General cargo; often out-of-gauge project cargo.
87: Vehicles are classed as DG by sea and air (UN3166 for fuel engines; UN3556 for lithium-ion electric). Parts are usually general cargo, except airbags (UN3268), batteries and fuel components.
88: Many aircraft parts are general cargo. Some contain DG: oxygen generators (UN3356), fire extinguishers (UN1044), life rafts (UN2990) and batteries.
89: General cargo; usually out-of-gauge or ro-ro. Boats with engines and fuel follow the vehicle rules.
90: Usually general cargo. Exceptions: mercury instruments (UN2809 / UN3506), devices with lithium batteries and magnetised parts (air).
91: General cargo; small button cells are normally exempt if protected.
93: Ammunition is Class 1 (e.g. UN0012 / UN0014). Arms need export and import licences, and most carriers need prior approval.
94: General cargo. Lamps with lithium batteries need a battery check.
95: Usually general cargo. Battery-operated toys, party poppers and gas-filled items need a check.
96: Usually general cargo. Lighters (9613) are DG (UN1057), and most airlines forbid them.
97: Not DG; valuable cargo (special handling, insurance, export permissions for antiques).

0303: Not DG. Frozen: -18°C reefer by sea; dry ice packing by air makes it DG (UN1845).
1203: Copra is self-heating, Class 4.2 (UN1363), by sea. Lines need DG booking and careful moisture control.
1207: Other oil seeds (castor, sesame, cotton seed etc.)
Castor beans are Class 9 (UN2969, toxic ricin content). Sesame, mustard and most other seeds are general cargo.
1302: Oleoresins or extracts with residual solvent may be flammable (Class 3, e.g. UN1169 / UN1197). Dry extracts and gums are general cargo.
1515: Castor oil and other vegetable oils are not DG.
2207: Ethanol is a flammable liquid, Class 3 (UN1170). Denatured spirit is also DG (UN1170 or UN1987).
2208: Alcoholic beverages: above 70% alcohol are Class 3 PG II and 24-70% are Class 3 PG III (UN3065). 24% or less is not regulated. By air, 24-70% in retail packs up to 5 L is normally not restricted.
2301: Fishmeal is DG unless stabilised and tested: UN2216 (stabilised, Class 9) or UN1374 (unstabilised, Class 4.2). Lines want an antioxidant / stabilisation certificate.
2302: Normally general cargo. Some lines ask for an oil-content or non-hazardous certificate for de-oiled rice bran.
2304: Solvent-extracted soybean meal with low oil and moisture is normally not DG, but lines ask for oil, moisture and solvent-free certificates. Otherwise it is seed cake, UN2217 (Class 4.2).
2306: Oil cake and seed cake (mustard, groundnut, cotton, castor meal)
Seed cake is self-heating, Class 4.2: UN1386 (higher oil content) or UN2217 (≤1.5% oil). Castor meal is UN2969 (Class 9). Many lines restrict it and want oil and moisture test certificates.
2503: Sulphur is Class 4.1 (UN1350). Prilled, granulated or flaked sulphur may be exempt by sea. Molten sulphur is UN2448.
2524: Asbestos is Class 9 (UN2212 amphibole / UN2590 chrysotile), and most countries ban or restrict its trade.
2620: Zinc ash (UN1435) and aluminium dross (UN3170) give off flammable gas when wet, Class 4.3. Other residues need an MSDS.
2701: In containers, coal is not under the DG code, but lines restrict it because of self-heating. It needs a declaration of temperature and moisture.
2707: Flammable liquids, Class 3 (UN1114 benzene, UN1294 toluene, UN1307 xylene).
2710: Petroleum oils: fuels, lubricants, base oils

Petrol (UN1203), diesel (UN1202), kerosene / ATF (UN1223 / UN1863) and solvents are Class 3. Lubricating oils, greases and base oils are usually not DG (high flash point), but some are marine pollutants. Check the MSDS.
2711: Flammable gases, Class 2.1 (UN1075 LPG, UN1978 propane, UN1011 butane, UN1971 / UN1972 natural gas).
2713: Not DG in solid form. Hot bitumen or cutback bitumen can be DG.
2715: Cutback bitumen or tar with solvent may be Class 3 (UN1999). Emulsions are usually not DG.
2801: Chlorine is a toxic gas (UN1017, Class 2.3), and iodine is Class 8 (UN3495).
2804: Hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, argon, silicon, phosphorus
Gases in cylinders are Class 2 (e.g. UN1066 nitrogen, UN1072 oxygen, UN1006 argon, UN1049 hydrogen). Silicon metal is normally not DG. Phosphorus is Class 4.2.
2808: Corrosive, Class 8, and an oxidiser when concentrated (UN2031).
2811: Hydrofluoric acid (UN1790) is highly dangerous and restricted. Many others are corrosive (Class 8). Some, like silicon dioxide, are not DG.
2814: Anhydrous ammonia is a toxic gas (UN1005, Class 2.3). Ammonia solution is UN2672 (Class 8).
2815: Corrosive, Class 8: caustic soda solid UN1823 / solution UN1824; caustic potash UN1813 / UN1814.
2817: Usually not DG, but it can be a marine pollutant (Class 9, UN3077) depending on the MSDS.
2827: Ferric chloride (UN1773 / UN2582) and zinc chloride (UN2331) are corrosive. Calcium chloride and sodium chloride are not DG.
2828: Calcium hypochlorite is an oxidiser, Class 5.1 (UN1748 / UN2880 / UN2208 / UN3485–3487), and several lines refuse or restrict it after ship fires. Sodium hypochlorite solution is Class 8 (UN1791).
2829: Oxidisers, Class 5.1 (UN1495 sodium chlorate, UN1489 potassium perchlorate).
2833: Most sulphates are not DG. Copper sulphate and some others are marine pollutants (UN3077).
2834: Most nitrates are oxidisers, Class 5.1 (UN1486 potassium nitrate, UN1498 sodium nitrate, UN1500 sodium nitrite).
2836: Soda ash and calcium carbonate are not DG.
2841: Potassium permanganate is an oxidiser (UN1490, Class 5.1). Dichromates are DG (oxidiser / toxic).
2847: Oxidiser, Class 5.1 (UN2014 / UN2015). Solutions under 8% are normally not regulated.
2849: Calcium carbide gives off flammable gas when wet, Class 4.3 (UN1402). Silicon carbide is not DG.
2902: Flammable liquids, Class 3 (UN1294, UN1307, UN2055, UN1114).
2905: Methanol (UN1230) and isopropyl alcohol (UN1219) are Class 3. Ethylene glycol, glycerol and sorbitol are normally not DG.
2909: Many ethers are flammable (Class 3). Check the MSDS.
2915: Glacial acetic acid is Class 8 (UN2789). Ethyl acetate (UN1173) and butyl acetate (UN1123) are Class 3. Many salts are not DG.
2933: Many APIs and intermediates are not DG, but some are toxic (Class 6.1) or marine pollutants. The MSDS decides.
3002: Vaccines are usually not DG but need a cool chain. Patient and diagnostic samples are UN3373 (Category B). Shipments with dry ice add UN1845.
3004: Finished medicines are usually general cargo; some need temperature control. Liquid formulations in alcohol or aerosol inhalers can be DG.
3006: Kits containing small amounts of DG are UN3316 (chemical kit / first aid kit). Otherwise they are general cargo.
3102: Urea is not DG. Ammonium nitrate (UN1942) and ammonium nitrate fertilisers (UN2067) are Class 5.1, and many lines restrict them.
3105: Usually not DG, though some NPK grades with ammonium nitrate are Class 5.1 or Class 9 (UN2071). Lines ask for an MSDS.
3204: Usually not DG. Some are marine pollutants (UN3077 / UN3082) or toxic; check the MSDS.
3209: Usually not DG. Lines still ask for the MSDS.
3210: Depends on the solvent; check the MSDS.
3214: Mostly not DG. Some solvent-based sealants are Class 3.
3215: Solvent-based printing inks are Class 3 (UN1210). Water-based inks and ink cartridges are usually not DG.
3301: Many essential oils (citrus, eucalyptus, peppermint, lemongrass) have low flash points, Class 3 (UN1169 / UN1197). Others (sandalwood, vetiver) are not DG. Several are also marine pollutants.
3302: Mixtures with alcohol or solvents are Class 3 (UN1197 / UN1169 / UN1266). Powdered flavours are not DG.
3303: Perfumes with alcohol are flammable, Class 3 (UN1266). Oil-based attars may not be DG, depending on flash point.
3304: Creams, lotions and powders are not DG. Nail polish and removers are Class 3 (UN1263 / UN1090 / UN1993), and sprays are aerosols (UN1950).
3305: Shampoos and oils are not DG. Hair sprays and mousse are aerosols (UN1950). Hair dyes with peroxide developers can be DG.
3307: Aerosol deodorants and fresheners are UN1950. Agarbatti, incense and dhoop are general cargo.
3402: Usually not DG. Some industrial surfactants and cleaners are corrosive (UN1760 / UN1719).
3405: Solvent-based polishes may be Class 3. Water-based ones are not DG.
3506: Solvent-based adhesives are Class 3 (UN1133). Water-based, PVA and hot-melt glues are not DG.
3604: Class 1 (e.g. UN0336 1.4G, UN0335 1.3G). Needs a PESO licence, and most lines and airlines refuse or need prior approval.
3605: Safety matches are Class 4.1 (UN1944). Strike-anywhere matches are UN1331.
3606: Lighter refills are UN1057 (Class 2.1), firelighters are Class 4.1 (UN2623), and liquid fuels are Class 3.
3707: Developers and fixers may be DG (Class 8 / 6.1).
3802: Can be self-heating, Class 4.2 (UN1362). It can be shipped as non-DG only with a test report (UN N.4 self-heating test) showing it passes. Lines will ask for it.
3808: Most pesticides are DG: toxic (Class 6.1), flammable or marine pollutants (UN3077 / UN3082). Mosquito coils are general cargo.
3811: Often flammable or marine pollutants; check the MSDS.
3819: Usually not DG (high flash point), but check the MSDS.
3820: Glycol-based coolants are normally not DG.
3822: Kits are often exempt or UN3316. Individual reagents may be DG.
3824: Other chemical products (incl. foundry, cement additives)
3826: Pure biodiesel usually has a high flash point and is not Class 3, but it may be a marine pollutant. Blends with diesel are UN1202.
3903: Expandable polystyrene beads give off flammable vapour, Class 9 (UN2211). General-purpose polystyrene granules are not DG.
3907: Liquid epoxy resins are often marine pollutants (UN3082). Resin solutions in styrene or solvent are Class 3 (UN1866). Solid granules are not DG.
3912: Nitrocellulose is DG, Class 4.1 (UN2556 / UN2557 / UN2059). Other cellulose ethers are not DG.
4005: Rubber solution in solvent is Class 3 (UN1287). Compounded rubber sheets are not DG.
4402: Self-heating, Class 4.2 (UN1361), unless a UN N.4 test report shows it passes. Many lines refuse charcoal or need a test report, packing and temperature declarations.
5201: Pressed bales to standard density are normally not DG. Loose cotton can be UN3360 (Class 4.1), and wet cotton is UN1365.
5202: Oily cotton waste is self-heating, Class 4.2 (UN1364).
7202: Ferrosilicon with 30–90% silicon is Class 4.3 (UN1408) and gives off flammable and toxic gas when wet. Lines ask for analysis certificates for other ferro-alloys.
7204: Generally not DG, but turnings, borings and shavings liable to self-heat are UN2793 (Class 4.2). Imported scrap into India needs a radiation check and pre-shipment inspection.
7205: Most are not DG, but fine reactive powders need a check.
7311: Empty, new, unused cylinders are general cargo. Filled cylinders, and empty uncleaned ones (residue), are DG (Class 2).
7603: Flammable solid, Class 4.1 (UN1309 coated) or 4.3 (UN1396 uncoated).
8104: Ingots are normally not DG. Turnings, ribbons and pellets are Class 4.1 (UN1869), and powder is Class 4.3 (UN1418).
8108: Solid titanium is not DG. Sponge and powder are flammable (UN2878 / UN2546).
8407: Engines are DG unless fully drained and certified: UN3528 (flammable liquid engine). A drained-and-clean certificate may allow non-DG shipping by some carriers.
8408: Engines are DG unless drained: UN3528 / UN3530. Lines and airlines may accept drained engines with a certificate.
8414: Usually general cargo. Units with refrigerant gas or lithium batteries need a check.
8415: Units pre-charged with refrigerant may be DG: UN2857 (non-flammable gas) or UN3358 (flammable refrigerant such as R290 / R32). Small household charges are often exempt by sea; airlines are stricter.
8418: Same as air conditioners: depends on the refrigerant type and charge (UN2857 / UN3358).
8424: Charged fire extinguishers are DG, Class 2.2 (UN1044). Sprayers without gas are general cargo.
8427: Treated as vehicles: UN3166 (fuel) or UN3556 / UN3171 (battery powered).
8429: Self-propelled machinery is UN3530 or a vehicle (UN3166) when fuel or batteries are fitted. Usually out-of-gauge.
8467: Cordless tools contain lithium batteries (UN3481). Petrol-driven tools are UN3528.
8471: With lithium batteries inside: UN3481 (PI 967 for air).
8501: Usually general cargo. Gensets with fuel or batteries are DG (UN3530 / UN3528).
8504: Power banks are lithium batteries on their own (UN3480, cargo aircraft only by air). Oil-filled transformers may need an MSDS for the oil.
8506: Lithium metal cells are UN3090 / UN3091. Alkaline and zinc-carbon cells are not DG if protected against short circuit.
8507: Lithium-ion: UN3480 / UN3481 (Class 9). Wet lead-acid: UN2794 (Class 8). Non-spillable lead-acid: UN2800 (often excepted). NiMH: UN3496 (sea only). Sodium-ion: UN3551.
8517: Phones and devices with lithium batteries: UN3481 (PI 967 by air, usually Section II).
8518: Large speakers with strong magnets may be magnetised material for air (UN2807). Wireless headphones contain lithium batteries.
8543: E-cigarettes and vapes contain lithium batteries (UN3481). Airlines restrict them and may need cargo aircraft only.
8548: Waste and damaged lithium batteries need special approval and are often forbidden by air. Lead-acid waste is UN2794. Hazardous waste rules (Basel) apply.
8703: UN3166 (petrol / diesel / CNG) or UN3556 (lithium-ion electric). Lines need the fuel tank near empty and batteries disconnected or charge-limited.
8711: UN3166 (fuel) or UN3556 (lithium-ion electric, incl. e-bikes and e-scooters). Many airlines refuse lithium vehicles.
8708: Most parts are general cargo. Airbag modules and seat-belt pretensioners are UN3268 (Class 9). Shock absorbers with gas, batteries and fuel pumps with residue need a check.
9018: Usually general cargo. Battery-powered devices: UN3481 / UN3091. Devices with gas cylinders are DG.
9025: Mercury instruments are DG (UN2809 / UN3506) and restricted by air.
9303: Not DG by themselves, but licence-controlled and often refused. Ammunition is Class 1.
9503: Usually general cargo. Toys with lithium batteries (UN3481) and chemistry sets (UN3316) need a check.
9505: Party poppers and sparklers are fireworks (Class 1). Other decorations are general cargo.
9613: UN1057, Class 2.1. Most airlines forbid lighters as cargo unless specially approved. By sea, lines need DG booking.
9616: Empty atomisers are general cargo. Filled perfume sprays are UN1266 or aerosols (UN1950).

P: Alcohol-based perfumes are flammable (UN1266, Class 3). Small retail bottles may qualify for limited-quantity rules. Oil-based attars may not be DG; check the flash point on the MSDS.
Aerosol cans are UN1950 (Class 2.1 or 2.2). Roll-ons and sticks are usually not DG.
Alcohol-based sanitiser (usually 60–80% ethanol or IPA) is a flammable liquid, Class 3. Non-alcohol sanitisers are not DG.
Flammable, Class 3. Small retail bottles may ship as limited quantity.
All aerosol cans are DG, UN1950 (Class 2.1 if flammable propellant, 2.2 otherwise).
Many essential oils have a flash point below 60°C, so they are Class 3. Some are also marine pollutants. The MSDS flash point decides.
Heavy essential oils (sandalwood, vetiver, rose, oud)
These often have high flash points and may be non-DG, but the MSDS must confirm it.
Mentha oil is often Class 3 or a marine pollutant. Menthol crystals are usually not DG.
UN2969, Class 9 (castor beans, meal, pomace, flake). Castor OIL is not DG.
Castor oil is not dangerous goods. Lines may still ask for an MSDS.

Self-heating, Class 4.2: UN1386 (oil >1.5%) or UN2217 (oil ≤1.5%, moisture ≤11%). Some solvent-extracted meals with very low oil can be shipped as non-DG with a certificate. Many lines restrict this cargo.
Normally accepted as non-DG with oil, moisture and solvent-free certificates. Otherwise it is UN2217.

UN1362 (Class 4.2) unless a UN N.4 test report shows it passes. With a valid report most lines accept it as non-DG.

Glacial acetic acid is Class 8 with Class 3 subsidiary. Dilute vinegar is not DG.
Oxidiser, Class 5.1 (with Class 8). Under 8% is normally not regulated.
Flammable liquid, Class 3 (with toxic subsidiary risk).
Solvent-based: UN1263, Class 3. Water-based (emulsion, acrylic) is usually not DG.
Usually not DG. Lines want the MSDS.
Solvent-based inks are UN1210, Class 3. Water-based and paste inks are often not DG.
Solvent-based adhesives are UN1133 (Class 3). Water-based (PVA) adhesives are not DG.

Most are DG: toxic (Class 6.1), flammable (Class 3) or environmentally hazardous (Class 9). Classification is product-specific.

Synthetic camphor is a flammable solid, Class 4.1 (UN2717).

Wet, spillable: UN2794 (Class 8). Sealed non-spillable (VRLA / SMF) can be UN2800 and may be excepted if they meet the vibration and pressure tests.

UN3496 by sea (Class 9). Not restricted by air if protected against short circuit.
